This is questionable because what is meant by the context is to inform about the tribe, and that is why he said after it: And Thamud who hewed out the rocks in the valley, meaning they cut the rocks in the valley. Ibn Abbas said that they carved them and pierced them, and this is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said. From this it is said Mujtaba An-Namar if they pierced them, and ajtaba Al-Thawb if you open the garment, and from this also the pocket is said. God Almighty said: And you carve out of the mountains, houses in a state of exultation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim recited here the words of the poet: Everything except God will perish, just as the living, the ugly, and the evil will perish. They struck every deaf Saada with strong hands and forearms Ibn Ishaq said: They were Arabs and their home was in Wadi Al-Qura. We have already mentioned the story of Aad in detail in Surat Al-A'raf, so there is no need to repeat it. God the Almighty says: And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The stakes are the soldiers who strengthen his authority. It is said that Pharaoh would stake their hands and feet to iron stakes, hanging them from them. Mujahid said the same: He would stake people with stakes. This is what Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said. Al-Suddi said: He would tie a man by each leg to a stake, then drop a huge rock on him to crush him. Qatadah said: We have been told that he had shelters and playgrounds under which he could play, made of stakes and ropes. Thabit Al-Bunani said on the authority of Abu Rafi: Pharaoh was called lord of the stakes because he drove four stakes for his wife, then placed a huge millstone on her back until she died. And the Almighty said: Those who transgressed in the land * And increased corruption therein meaning they rebelled, acted insolently, and spread corruption and harm to people on earth so your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment meaning He sent down upon them a punishment from the sky and brought down upon them a punishment that cannot be averted from the criminal people. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Ibn Abbas said: He hears and sees, meaning He watches His creation in what they do and rewards each one according to his efforts in this world and the next. He will present all of creation before Him, and He will judge them justly and will reward each one according to what he deserves. He is far removed from injustice and oppression. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here a very strange hadith, and its chain of transmission and authenticity are questionable. He said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us, Yunus al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza al-Baisani, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Muadh, the believer is a prisoner before the Truth. O Muadh, the believer will not be at peace and will not feel safe from its turmoil until he leaves the bridge of Hell behind him. O Muadh, the Quran has restrained the believer from many of his desires and from being destroyed by them, by God’s permission. So the Quran is his guide, fear is his path, longing is his mount, prayer is his refuge, fasting is his paradise, charity is his release, truthfulness is his commander, modesty is his minister, and his Lord, the Almighty, is watching over all of that.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus Al-Hadha’ and Abu Hamza are unknown, and Abu Hamza on the authority of Muadh is mursal. And if it was from Abu Hamza, it would have been good, meaning if it was from his words, it would have been good. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sufyan ibn Salih told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, from Sufyan ibn Amr, from Aifa’, from Ibn Abd Al-Kila’i, that he heard him while he was preaching to the people, saying: Hell has seven bridges. He said: And the Sirat is over them. He said: Then the creation will be stopped at the first bridge and he will say: Stop them, for they will be questioned. He said: Then they will be held accountable for the prayer and asked about it. He said: Then those who perish will perish therein and those who are saved will be saved. Then when they reach the second bridge, they will be held accountable for the trust, how they fulfilled it and how they betrayed it. He said: Then those who perish will perish and those who are saved will be saved. Then when they reach the third bridge, they will be asked about the ties of kinship, how they maintained them and how they severed them. He said: Then those who perish will perish and those who are saved will be saved. He said: And the ties of kinship on that Day will hang down to the depths in Hell, saying: O God, whoever maintains ties with me, sever them, and whoever severs ties with me, sever them. He said: And it is about which God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. This is how it was reported. This trace is not mentioned in full.
89:13: As for Fajr, it is well-known and is the morning. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Al-Suddi said this. On the authority of Masruq and Muhammad ibn Ka’b: What is meant by it is the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice specifically, and it is the last of the ten nights. It was also said that what is meant by it is the prayer that is performed on it, as Ikrimah said. It was also said that what is meant by it is the entire day, and this is a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The ten nights mean the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, as Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and more than one of the early and later generations said. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to God than these days, meaning the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. They said: Not even jihad in the cause of God? He said: Not even jihad in the cause of God, except for a man who goes out with himself and his wealth and does not return with anything of it.” It was also said that what is meant by this is the first ten days of Muharram. Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir narrated it and did not attribute it to anyone. Abu Kudayna narrated on the authority of Qabus ibn Abi Dhibyan on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And ten nights. He said: It is the first ten days of Ramadan, and the first statement is correct. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, Ayyash bin Uqba told us, Khair bin Naim told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: The ten are the ten days of sacrifice, the odd is the day of Arafah, and the even is the day of sacrifice. An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ and Abdah bin Abdullah, and each of them on the authority of Zaid bin Al-Hubab with it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Zaid bin Al-Hubab with it. The men in this chain of transmission are acceptable, but I believe that the text in its being attributed to the Prophet is strange, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And the even and the odd. It was mentioned in this hadith that the even is the Day of Arafah because it is the ninth, and that the even is the Day of Sacrifice because it is the tenth. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ad-Dahhak also said this a second saying. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Uqbah bin Khalid told me on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa’ib, who said: I asked Ata’ about the Almighty’s saying: And the even and the odd. I said: Is this our prayer and our odd? He said: No, but the even is on the Day of Arafah and the odd is on the Night of Sacrifice. A third opinion Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Asbahani told us, my father told me on the authority of al-Nu’man, meaning Ibn Abd al-Salam, on the authority of Abu Sa’id ibn Awf, who told me in Mecca: I heard Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr delivering a sermon to the people, and a man stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the even and the odd. He said: The even is the statement of God the Most High: But whoever hastens to pray in two days, there is no sin upon him and the odd is the statement of God the Most High: And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. Ibn Jurayj said: Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi’ told me that he heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: The even is the middle of the days of Tashreeq and the odd is the last of the days of Tashreeq. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. He is odd and loves odd numbers.” Fourth statement Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Zaid bin Aslam said: All creation is even and odd. God swears by His creation. This is a narration from Mujahid, and the first is the most well-known from him. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: And even and odd he said: God is odd and one, and you are even. It is said that even is the dawn prayer and odd is the sunset prayer. Fifth statement Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, By the even and the odd, he said: The even is the pair, and the odd is God, the Almighty. Abu Abdullah said on the authority of Mujahid: God is the odd, and He created the even, male and female. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: By the even and the odd, everything that God created is even: the sky, the earth, the land, the sea, the jinn, mankind, the sun, the moon, and so on. Mujahid followed in this what they mentioned in the statement of God, the Almighty: And of everything We have created pairs that you may remember, meaning so that you may know that the Creator of pairs is One. Sixth statement Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan: The even and the odd are the number, some of which are even and some are odd. Seventh statement on the noble verse Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Then Ibn Jarir said: A narration was narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that supports the statement we mentioned on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr. Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani told me, Zayd ibn al-Habbab told us, Ayyash ibn Uqba told me, Khair ibn Na’eem told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The even shafa’ is the two days and the odd witr is the third day. This is how this narration was narrated with this wording, and it contradicts the previous wording in the narration of Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Abi Hatim, and what he also narrated, and God knows best. Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and others said: It is the prayer, some of which is even, like the four-rak’ah and two-rak’ah prayer, and some of which is odd, like the Maghrib prayer, which is three and is the odd witr of the day. The same applies to the witr prayer at the end of the night prayer. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, And the even and the odd. He said, It is the obligatory prayer, some of which are even and some of which are odd. This is a disconnected and suspended hadith, and its wording is specific to the obligatory prayer. It has been narrated in a continuous chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its wording is general. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Dawud - he is At-Tayalisi - told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, that a sheikh from the people of Basra told him, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, that the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - was asked about the even and the witr, so he said: It is the prayer, partly even and partly witr. This is how it appears in Al-Musnad. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Affan, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Musa, and both of them narrated it from Hammam - he is Ibn Yahya - on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of a sheikh, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. Abu Isa At-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Amr bin Ali, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi and Abu Dawud - both of them on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of a man from the people of Basra, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, with this chain of transmission. Then he said: It is strange, we do not know it except from the hadith of Qatadah. Khalid bin Qais also narrated it on the authority of Qatadah, and it was narrated on the authority of Imran bin Issam on the authority of Imran himself, and God knows best. I said: It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: Ahmad bin Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Imran bin Issam al-Dab’i, a sheikh from the people of Basra, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. This is how I saw it in his interpretation, so he made the sheikh from Basra to be Imran bin Issam. And this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it: Nasr bin Ali told us, my father told me, Khalid bin Qais told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the even and the odd, he said: It is the prayer, some of it is even and some of it is odd, so he omitted the mention of the unknown sheikh, and Imran bin Issam al-Dab’i Abu Amara al-Basri, the imam of the mosque of Bani Dabi’ah, is the only one who narrated it. He is the father of Abu Jamrah Nasr ibn Imran al-Dab’i. Qatada, his son Abu Jamrah, al-Muthanna ibn Sa’id, and Abu al-Tayyah Yazid ibn Hamid narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in the Book of Trustworthy People, and Khalifah ibn Khayyat mentioned him among the Tabi’in from the people of Basra. He was a noble and honorable man who was favored by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, then he was killed on the day of al-Zawiya in the year 83 AH for going out with Ibn al-Ash’ath. He has no narration with al-Tirmidhi except this one hadith, and I think that stopping it with Imran ibn Husayn is more likely, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir did not assert any of these statements regarding the even and odd numbers. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And the night when it departs} Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning when it goes away. Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr said: {And the night when it departs} until some parts of it go away. Mujahid, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Qatadah and Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Zayd: {And the night when it departs} when it goes. This can be interpreted as what Ibn Abbas said, meaning it goes away. It is possible that what is meant is when it departs, meaning it approaches. It may be said that this is more appropriate because it is in opposition to His saying: {And the dawn}, for dawn is the approach of the day and the departure of the night. So if His saying: {And the night when it departs} is interpreted as its approach, then it is an oath by the approach of the night and the departure of the day and vice versa, like His saying: {And the night when it covers a deep darkness * And the morning when it breathes}. Ad-Dahhak also said: {And the night when it departs} meaning it runs. Ikrimah said: {And the night when it departs} meaning the night of Muzdalifah. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Issam told us, Abu Amir told us, on the authority of Katheer bin Abdullah bin Amr, who said: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say regarding His statement: And the night when it departs, he said: Travel, O traveler, and do not spend the night except in a group. And the statement of God Almighty: Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? That is, for one of reason, intelligence, religion, and wisdom. Reason is called a stone because it prevents a person from engaging in actions and words that are not appropriate for him. And from this is the stone of the House because it prevents the circumambulator from sticking to its Syrian wall, and from this is the stone of Yamamah, and the ruler’s stone on someone if he prevents him from acting. And they say, ‘A forbidden stone.’ All of this is of one type, and has a close meaning. This oath is by the times of worship and by the worship itself of Hajj, prayer, and other types of closeness by which His pious and obedient servants draw near to Him, who fear Him, are humble before Him, and are submissive to His noble face. And when He mentioned these people and their worship and obedience, He said after that: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the ‘Aad? And these people were rebellious. They were tyrants and oppressors who disobeyed Him, belied His messengers and rejected His books. So God the Almighty mentioned how He destroyed them and made them stories and lessons, saying: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, * Iram, who had lofty pillars? These were the first ‘Aad, and they were the descendants of ‘Aad, son of Iram, son of Aws, son of Sam, son of Noah, as Ibn Ishaq said. They were the ones among whom God sent His Messenger Hud, peace be upon him, but they belied him and opposed him. So God saved him from among them and those who believed with him from among them and destroyed them “with a furious, violent wind, which He subjected to them for seven nights and eight days in succession. So you would see the people therein fallen down as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. So do you see any remnant of them?” God the Almighty mentioned their story in the Qur’an in more than one place so that the believers would take heed from their destruction. So His statement, Iram, who had lofty pillars, is an explanatory apposition to further define them. God the Almighty said: of the pillars because they used to live in tents raised by strong pillars. They were the strongest people of their time in creation and the most powerful in strength. For this reason, Hud reminded them of that blessing and guided them to use it in obeying their Lord who created them. He said: “And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature abundantly. So remember the favors of God that you may succeed.” And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. God the Almighty said: As for ‘Aad, they were arrogant upon the land without right and said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ Did they not see that God, who created them, was stronger than them in strength? And He said here: whose like had not been created in the lands, meaning the tribe whose like had not been created in their land due to their strength, strength, and great composition. Mujahid said: Iram was an ancient nation, meaning the first ‘Aad. Qatada bin Di’amah and Al-Suddi said: Iram was the house of the kingdom of ‘Aad. This is a good, good and strong statement. Mujahid, Qatada and Al-Kalbi said regarding His statement: of the pillars that they were people of pillars who did not stand. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were called of the pillars because of their height. Ibn Jarir chose the first and rejected the second and he was correct. And the Almighty’s saying: The like of which has not been created in the land, Ibn Zayd returned the pronoun to the pillars because of their height and said: They built pillars in Al-Ahqaf, the like of which has not been created in the land. As for Qatada and Ibn Jarir, they returned the pronoun to the tribe, meaning the like of that tribe has not been created in the land, meaning in their time. This statement is correct, and the statement of Ibn Zayd and those who followed his school is weak because if that was what was meant, he would have said the like of which has not been created in the land, but rather he said: The like of which has not been created in the land. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Al-Miqdam, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he mentioned Iram of the Pillars and said: A man from them would come to the rock and carry it against the tribe, destroying them. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Abu Al-Tahir told us, Anas bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Thawr bin Zayd Al-Dailami, who said: I read a book and he named where he read it, I am Shaddad bin Aad, and I am the one who raised the pillars, and I am He who strengthened with my two arms the sight of one, and I am the one who hoarded a treasure of seven cubits that none can extract except the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: According to every statement, whether the pillars were buildings that they built or the columns of their homes for the Bedouins or a weapon with which they fought or the height of one of them, they are a tribe and a nation among the nations, and they are the ones mentioned in the Qur’an in more than one place, paired with Thamud as here, and God knows best. Whoever claims that what is meant by His statement, Iram of the Pillars, is a city, either Damascus, as narrated by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ikrimah, or Alexandria, as narrated by Al-Qurazi or others, then there is a problem with that, because how can the statement be consistent with this, Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, * Iram of the Pillars? If that is made a substitute or an explanatory apposition, then the statement is not consistent in that case. Then what is meant is only the report of the destruction of the tribe called ‘Aad and what God brought upon them of His punishment that cannot be averted, not that what is meant is the report of a city or a region. I have only drawn attention to this so that one will not be deceived by much of what a group of commentators have mentioned regarding this verse, of a city called Iram of the Pillars, built with bricks of gold and silver, its palaces, houses, and orchards, and that its pebbles are pearls and jewels, its soil is musk, its rivers are flowing, its fruits are falling, its houses have no companions, its walls and gates are yellow, there is no one to call or answer it, and that it moves, sometimes being in the land of Syria, sometimes in Yemen, sometimes in Iraq, and sometimes in other countries. All of this is from the fables of the Israelites, made up by some of their heretics, to test the minds of the ignorant among the people, to make them believe them in all of that. Al-Tha’labi and others mentioned that a Bedouin man, Abdullah bin Qilabah, went in search of his camels during the time of Mu’awiyah, and while he was wandering in search of them, he saw a great city with walls and gates. He entered it and found in it something close to what we mentioned of the characteristics of the golden city that was mentioned earlier. He returned and informed the people, and they went with him to the place he had mentioned, but they did not see anything. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned the story of Iram of the Pillars here at length, and this story cannot be attributed correctly. Even if it were true that the Bedouin was the one who invented it, he might have invented it or he might have been afflicted with a kind of delusion and madness, so he believed that it was real in the outside world, but it was not. This is what makes it certain that it is not true. This is similar to what many of the ignorant, greedy, and deceitful people say about the existence of underground treasures, containing tons of gold and silver, various types of jewels, rubies, pearls, and great elixirs, but there are obstacles that prevent access to them and taking from them. They deceive the money of the rich, the weak, and the foolish, and they eat it unjustly by spending it on intoxicants, drugs, and similar nonsense, and they joke about them. What is certain is that there are pre-Islamic and Islamic treasures in the earth, and whoever obtains something from them can convert it. As for the way they claimed, it is a lie, slander, and defamation, and nothing of what they say is authentic except from their own transmission or the transmission of someone who took from them. And God… Glory be to Him, the Most High, the Guide to the Right Path. Ibn Jarir’s statement: It is possible that what is meant by his saying: Iram of the Pillars is a tribe or a town that Ad inhabited, and that is why it was not declined. This is questionable because what is meant by the context is to inform about the tribe, and that is why he said after it: And Thamud who hewed out the rocks in the valley, meaning they cut the rocks in the valley. Ibn Abbas said that they carved them and pierced them, and this is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said. From this it is said Mujtaba An-Namar if they pierced them, and ajtaba Al-Thawb if you open the garment, and from this also the pocket is said. God Almighty said: And you carve out of the mountains, houses in a state of exultation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim recited here the words of the poet: Everything except God will perish, just as the living, the ugly, and the evil will perish. They struck every deaf Saada with strong hands and forearms Ibn Ishaq said: They were Arabs and their home was in Wadi Al-Qura. We have already mentioned the story of Aad in detail in Surat Al-A'raf, so there is no need to repeat it. God the Almighty says: And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The stakes are the soldiers who strengthen his authority. It is said that Pharaoh would stake their hands and feet to iron stakes, hanging them from them. Mujahid said the same: He would stake people with stakes. This is what Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said. Al-Suddi said: He would tie a man by each leg to a stake, then drop a huge rock on him to crush him. Qatadah said: We have been told that he had shelters and playgrounds under which he could play, made of stakes and ropes. Thabit Al-Bunani said on the authority of Abu Rafi: Pharaoh was called lord of the stakes because he drove four stakes for his wife, then placed a huge millstone on her back until she died. And the Almighty said: Those who transgressed in the land * And increased corruption therein meaning they rebelled, acted insolently, and spread corruption and harm to people on earth so your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment meaning He sent down upon them a punishment from the sky and brought down upon them a punishment that cannot be averted from the criminal people. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Ibn Abbas said: He hears and sees, meaning He watches His creation in what they do and rewards each one according to his efforts in this world and the next. He will present all of creation before Him, and He will judge them justly and will reward each one according to what he deserves. He is far removed from injustice and oppression. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here a very strange hadith, and its chain of transmission and authenticity are questionable. He said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us, Yunus al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza al-Baisani, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Muadh, the believer is a prisoner before the Truth. O Muadh, the believer will not be at peace and will not feel safe from its turmoil until he leaves the bridge of Hell behind him. O Muadh, the Quran has restrained the believer from many of his desires and from being destroyed by them, by God’s permission. So the Quran is his guide, fear is his path, longing is his mount, prayer is his refuge, fasting is his paradise, charity is his release, truthfulness is his commander, modesty is his minister, and his Lord, the Almighty, is watching over all of that.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus Al-Hadha’ and Abu Hamza are unknown, and Abu Hamza on the authority of Muadh is mursal. And if it was from Abu Hamza, it would have been good, meaning if it was from his words, it would have been good. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sufyan ibn Salih told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, from Sufyan ibn Amr, from Aifa’, from Ibn Abd Al-Kila’i, that he heard him while he was preaching to the people, saying: Hell has seven bridges. He said: And the Sirat is over them. He said: Then the creation will be stopped at the first bridge and he will say: Stop them, for they will be questioned. He said: Then they will be held accountable for the prayer and asked about it. He said: Then those who perish will perish therein and those who are saved will be saved. Then when they reach the second bridge, they will be held accountable for the trust, how they fulfilled it and how they betrayed it. He said: Then those who perish will perish and those who are saved will be saved. Then when they reach the third bridge, they will be asked about the ties of kinship, how they maintained them and how they severed them. He said: Then those who perish will perish and those who are saved will be saved. He said: And the ties of kinship on that Day will hang down to the depths in Hell, saying: O God, whoever maintains ties with me, sever them, and whoever severs ties with me, sever them. He said: And it is about which God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. This is how it was reported. This trace is not mentioned in full.
89:14: As for Fajr, it is well-known and is the morning. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Al-Suddi said this. On the authority of Masruq and Muhammad ibn Ka’b: What is meant by it is the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice specifically, and it is the last of the ten nights. It was also said that what is meant by it is the prayer that is performed on it, as Ikrimah said. It was also said that what is meant by it is the entire day, and this is a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The ten nights mean the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, as Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and more than one of the early and later generations said. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to God than these days, meaning the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. They said: Not even jihad in the cause of God? He said: Not even jihad in the cause of God, except for a man who goes out with himself and his wealth and does not return with anything of it.” It was also said that what is meant by this is the first ten days of Muharram. Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir narrated it and did not attribute it to anyone. Abu Kudayna narrated on the authority of Qabus ibn Abi Dhibyan on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And ten nights. He said: It is the first ten days of Ramadan, and the first statement is correct. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, Ayyash bin Uqba told us, Khair bin Naim told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: The ten are the ten days of sacrifice, the odd is the day of Arafah, and the even is the day of sacrifice. An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ and Abdah bin Abdullah, and each of them on the authority of Zaid bin Al-Hubab with it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Zaid bin Al-Hubab with it. The men in this chain of transmission are acceptable, but I believe that the text in its being attributed to the Prophet is strange, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And the even and the odd. It was mentioned in this hadith that the even is the Day of Arafah because it is the ninth, and that the even is the Day of Sacrifice because it is the tenth. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ad-Dahhak also said this a second saying. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Uqbah bin Khalid told me on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa’ib, who said: I asked Ata’ about the Almighty’s saying: And the even and the odd. I said: Is this our prayer and our odd? He said: No, but the even is on the Day of Arafah and the odd is on the Night of Sacrifice. A third opinion Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Asbahani told us, my father told me on the authority of al-Nu’man, meaning Ibn Abd al-Salam, on the authority of Abu Sa’id ibn Awf, who told me in Mecca: I heard Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr delivering a sermon to the people, and a man stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the even and the odd. He said: The even is the statement of God the Most High: But whoever hastens to pray in two days, there is no sin upon him and the odd is the statement of God the Most High: And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. Ibn Jurayj said: Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi’ told me that he heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: The even is the middle of the days of Tashreeq and the odd is the last of the days of Tashreeq. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. He is odd and loves odd numbers.” Fourth statement Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Zaid bin Aslam said: All creation is even and odd. God swears by His creation. This is a narration from Mujahid, and the first is the most well-known from him. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: And even and odd he said: God is odd and one, and you are even. It is said that even is the dawn prayer and odd is the sunset prayer. Fifth statement Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, By the even and the odd, he said: The even is the pair, and the odd is God, the Almighty. Abu Abdullah said on the authority of Mujahid: God is the odd, and He created the even, male and female. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: By the even and the odd, everything that God created is even: the sky, the earth, the land, the sea, the jinn, mankind, the sun, the moon, and so on. Mujahid followed in this what they mentioned in the statement of God, the Almighty: And of everything We have created pairs that you may remember, meaning so that you may know that the Creator of pairs is One. Sixth statement Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan: The even and the odd are the number, some of which are even and some are odd. Seventh statement on the noble verse Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Then Ibn Jarir said: A narration was narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that supports the statement we mentioned on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr. Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani told me, Zayd ibn al-Habbab told us, Ayyash ibn Uqba told me, Khair ibn Na’eem told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The even shafa’ is the two days and the odd witr is the third day. This is how this narration was narrated with this wording, and it contradicts the previous wording in the narration of Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Abi Hatim, and what he also narrated, and God knows best. Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and others said: It is the prayer, some of which is even, like the four-rak’ah and two-rak’ah prayer, and some of which is odd, like the Maghrib prayer, which is three and is the odd witr of the day. The same applies to the witr prayer at the end of the night prayer. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, And the even and the odd. He said, It is the obligatory prayer, some of which are even and some of which are odd. This is a disconnected and suspended hadith, and its wording is specific to the obligatory prayer. It has been narrated in a continuous chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its wording is general. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Dawud - he is At-Tayalisi - told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, that a sheikh from the people of Basra told him, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, that the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - was asked about the even and the witr, so he said: It is the prayer, partly even and partly witr. This is how it appears in Al-Musnad. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Affan, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Musa, and both of them narrated it from Hammam - he is Ibn Yahya - on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of a sheikh, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. Abu Isa At-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Amr bin Ali, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi and Abu Dawud - both of them on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of a man from the people of Basra, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, with this chain of transmission. Then he said: It is strange, we do not know it except from the hadith of Qatadah. Khalid bin Qais also narrated it on the authority of Qatadah, and it was narrated on the authority of Imran bin Issam on the authority of Imran himself, and God knows best. I said: It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: Ahmad bin Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Imran bin Issam al-Dab’i, a sheikh from the people of Basra, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. This is how I saw it in his interpretation, so he made the sheikh from Basra to be Imran bin Issam. And this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it: Nasr bin Ali told us, my father told me, Khalid bin Qais told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the even and the odd, he said: It is the prayer, some of it is even and some of it is odd, so he omitted the mention of the unknown sheikh, and Imran bin Issam al-Dab’i Abu Amara al-Basri, the imam of the mosque of Bani Dabi’ah, is the only one who narrated it. He is the father of Abu Jamrah Nasr ibn Imran al-Dab’i. Qatada, his son Abu Jamrah, al-Muthanna ibn Sa’id, and Abu al-Tayyah Yazid ibn Hamid narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in the Book of Trustworthy People, and Khalifah ibn Khayyat mentioned him among the Tabi’in from the people of Basra. He was a noble and honorable man who was favored by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, then he was killed on the day of al-Zawiya in the year 83 AH for going out with Ibn al-Ash’ath. He has no narration with al-Tirmidhi except this one hadith, and I think that stopping it with Imran ibn Husayn is more likely, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir did not assert any of these statements regarding the even and odd numbers. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And the night when it departs} Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning when it goes away. Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr said: {And the night when it departs} until some parts of it go away. Mujahid, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Qatadah and Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Zayd: {And the night when it departs} when it goes. This can be interpreted as what Ibn Abbas said, meaning it goes away. It is possible that what is meant is when it departs, meaning it approaches. It may be said that this is more appropriate because it is in opposition to His saying: {And the dawn}, for dawn is the approach of the day and the departure of the night. So if His saying: {And the night when it departs} is interpreted as its approach, then it is an oath by the approach of the night and the departure of the day and vice versa, like His saying: {And the night when it covers a deep darkness * And the morning when it breathes}. Ad-Dahhak also said: {And the night when it departs} meaning it runs. Ikrimah said: {And the night when it departs} meaning the night of Muzdalifah. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Issam told us, Abu Amir told us, on the authority of Katheer bin Abdullah bin Amr, who said: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say regarding His statement: And the night when it departs, he said: Travel, O traveler, and do not spend the night except in a group. And the statement of God Almighty: Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? That is, for one of reason, intelligence, religion, and wisdom. Reason is called a stone because it prevents a person from engaging in actions and words that are not appropriate for him. And from this is the stone of the House because it prevents the circumambulator from sticking to its Syrian wall, and from this is the stone of Yamamah, and the ruler’s stone on someone if he prevents him from acting. And they say, ‘A forbidden stone.’ All of this is of one type, and has a close meaning. This oath is by the times of worship and by the worship itself of Hajj, prayer, and other types of closeness by which His pious and obedient servants draw near to Him, who fear Him, are humble before Him, and are submissive to His noble face. And when He mentioned these people and their worship and obedience, He said after that: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the ‘Aad? And these people were rebellious. They were tyrants and oppressors who disobeyed Him, belied His messengers and rejected His books. So God the Almighty mentioned how He destroyed them and made them stories and lessons, saying: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, * Iram, who had lofty pillars? These were the first ‘Aad, and they were the descendants of ‘Aad, son of Iram, son of Aws, son of Sam, son of Noah, as Ibn Ishaq said. They were the ones among whom God sent His Messenger Hud, peace be upon him, but they belied him and opposed him. So God saved him from among them and those who believed with him from among them and destroyed them “with a furious, violent wind, which He subjected to them for seven nights and eight days in succession. So you would see the people therein fallen down as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. So do you see any remnant of them?” God the Almighty mentioned their story in the Qur’an in more than one place so that the believers would take heed from their destruction. So His statement, Iram, who had lofty pillars, is an explanatory apposition to further define them. God the Almighty said: of the pillars because they used to live in tents raised by strong pillars. They were the strongest people of their time in creation and the most powerful in strength. For this reason, Hud reminded them of that blessing and guided them to use it in obeying their Lord who created them. He said: “And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature abundantly. So remember the favors of God that you may succeed.” And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. God the Almighty said: As for ‘Aad, they were arrogant upon the land without right and said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ Did they not see that God, who created them, was stronger than them in strength? And He said here: whose like had not been created in the lands, meaning the tribe whose like had not been created in their land due to their strength, strength, and great composition. Mujahid said: Iram was an ancient nation, meaning the first ‘Aad. Qatada bin Di’amah and Al-Suddi said: Iram was the house of the kingdom of ‘Aad. This is a good, good and strong statement. Mujahid, Qatada and Al-Kalbi said regarding His statement: of the pillars that they were people of pillars who did not stand. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were called of the pillars because of their height. Ibn Jarir chose the first and rejected the second and he was correct. And the Almighty’s saying: The like of which has not been created in the land, Ibn Zayd returned the pronoun to the pillars because of their height and said: They built pillars in Al-Ahqaf, the like of which has not been created in the land. As for Qatada and Ibn Jarir, they returned the pronoun to the tribe, meaning the like of that tribe has not been created in the land, meaning in their time. This statement is correct, and the statement of Ibn Zayd and those who followed his school is weak because if that was what was meant, he would have said the like of which has not been created in the land, but rather he said: The like of which has not been created in the land. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Al-Miqdam, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he mentioned Iram of the Pillars and said: A man from them would come to the rock and carry it against the tribe, destroying them. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Abu Al-Tahir told us, Anas bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Thawr bin Zayd Al-Dailami, who said: I read a book and he named where he read it, I am Shaddad bin Aad, and I am the one who raised the pillars, and I am He who strengthened with my two arms the sight of one, and I am the one who hoarded a treasure of seven cubits that none can extract except the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: According to every statement, whether the pillars were buildings that they built or the columns of their homes for the Bedouins or a weapon with which they fought or the height of one of them, they are a tribe and a nation among the nations, and they are the ones mentioned in the Qur’an in more than one place, paired with Thamud as here, and God knows best. Whoever claims that what is meant by His statement, Iram of the Pillars, is a city, either Damascus, as narrated by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ikrimah, or Alexandria, as narrated by Al-Qurazi or others, then there is a problem with that, because how can the statement be consistent with this, Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, * Iram of the Pillars? If that is made a substitute or an explanatory apposition, then the statement is not consistent in that case. Then what is meant is only the report of the destruction of the tribe called ‘Aad and what God brought upon them of His punishment that cannot be averted, not that what is meant is the report of a city or a region. I have only drawn attention to this so that one will not be deceived by much of what a group of commentators have mentioned regarding this verse, of a city called Iram of the Pillars, built with bricks of gold and silver, its palaces, houses, and orchards, and that its pebbles are pearls and jewels, its soil is musk, its rivers are flowing, its fruits are falling, its houses have no companions, its walls and gates are yellow, there is no one to call or answer it, and that it moves, sometimes being in the land of Syria, sometimes in Yemen, sometimes in Iraq, and sometimes in other countries. All of this is from the fables of the Israelites, made up by some of their heretics, to test the minds of the ignorant among the people, to make them believe them in all of that. Al-Tha’labi and others mentioned that a Bedouin man, Abdullah bin Qilabah, went in search of his camels during the time of Mu’awiyah, and while he was wandering in search of them, he saw a great city with walls and gates. He entered it and found in it something close to what we mentioned of the characteristics of the golden city that was mentioned earlier. He returned and informed the people, and they went with him to the place he had mentioned, but they did not see anything. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned the story of Iram of the Pillars here at length, and this story cannot be attributed correctly. Even if it were true that the Bedouin was the one who invented it, he might have invented it or he might have been afflicted with a kind of delusion and madness, so he believed that it was real in the outside world, but it was not. This is what makes it certain that it is not true. This is similar to what many of the ignorant, greedy, and deceitful people say about the existence of underground treasures, containing tons of gold and silver, various types of jewels, rubies, pearls, and great elixirs, but there are obstacles that prevent access to them and taking from them. They deceive the money of the rich, the weak, and the foolish, and they eat it unjustly by spending it on intoxicants, drugs, and similar nonsense, and they joke about them. What is certain is that there are pre-Islamic and Islamic treasures in the earth, and whoever obtains something from them can convert it. As for the way they claimed, it is a lie, slander, and defamation, and nothing of what they say is authentic except from their own transmission or the transmission of someone who took from them. And God… Glory be to Him, the Most High, the Guide to the Right Path. Ibn Jarir’s statement: It is possible that what is meant by his saying: Iram of the Pillars is a tribe or a town that Ad inhabited, and that is why it was not declined. This is questionable because what is meant by the context is to inform about the tribe, and that is why he said after it: And Thamud who hewed out the rocks in the valley, meaning they cut the rocks in the valley. Ibn Abbas said that they carved them and pierced them, and this is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said. From this it is said Mujtaba An-Namar if they pierced them, and ajtaba Al-Thawb if you open the garment, and from this also the pocket is said. God Almighty said: And you carve out of the mountains, houses in a state of exultation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim recited here the words of the poet: Everything except God will perish, just as the living, the ugly, and the evil will perish. They struck every deaf Saada with strong hands and forearms Ibn Ishaq said: They were Arabs and their home was in Wadi Al-Qura. We have already mentioned the story of Aad in detail in Surat Al-A'raf, so there is no need to repeat it. God the Almighty says: And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The stakes are the soldiers who strengthen his authority. It is said that Pharaoh would stake their hands and feet to iron stakes, hanging them from them. Mujahid said the same: He would stake people with stakes. This is what Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said. Al-Suddi said: He would tie a man by each leg to a stake, then drop a huge rock on him to crush him. Qatadah said: We have been told that he had shelters and playgrounds under which he could play, made of stakes and ropes. Thabit Al-Bunani said on the authority of Abu Rafi: Pharaoh was called lord of the stakes because he drove four stakes for his wife, then placed a huge millstone on her back until she died. And the Almighty said: Those who transgressed in the land * And increased corruption therein meaning they rebelled, acted insolently, and spread corruption and harm to people on earth so your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment meaning He sent down upon them a punishment from the sky and brought down upon them a punishment that cannot be averted from the criminal people. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Ibn Abbas said: He hears and sees, meaning He watches His creation in what they do and rewards each one according to his efforts in this world and the next. He will present all of creation before Him, and He will judge them justly and will reward each one according to what he deserves. He is far removed from injustice and oppression. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here a very strange hadith, and its chain of transmission and authenticity are questionable. He said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us, Yunus al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza al-Baisani, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Muadh, the believer is a prisoner before the Truth. O Muadh, the believer will not be at peace and will not feel safe from its turmoil until he leaves the bridge of Hell behind him. O Muadh, the Quran has restrained the believer from many of his desires and from being destroyed by them, by God’s permission. So the Quran is his guide, fear is his path, longing is his mount, prayer is his refuge, fasting is his paradise, charity is his release, truthfulness is his commander, modesty is his minister, and his Lord, the Almighty, is watching over all of that.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus Al-Hadha’ and Abu Hamza are unknown, and Abu Hamza on the authority of Muadh is mursal. And if it was from Abu Hamza, it would have been good, meaning if it was from his words, it would have been good. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sufyan ibn Salih told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, from Sufyan ibn Amr, from Aifa’, from Ibn Abd Al-Kila’i, that he heard him while he was preaching to the people, saying: Hell has seven bridges. He said: And the Sirat is over them. He said: Then the creation will be stopped at the first bridge and he will say: Stop them, for they will be questioned. He said: Then they will be held accountable for the prayer and asked about it. He said: Then those who perish will perish therein and those who are saved will be saved. Then when they reach the second bridge, they will be held accountable for the trust, how they fulfilled it and how they betrayed it. He said: Then those who perish will perish and those who are saved will be saved. Then when they reach the third bridge, they will be asked about the ties of kinship, how they maintained them and how they severed them. He said: Then those who perish will perish and those who are saved will be saved. He said: And the ties of kinship on that Day will hang down to the depths in Hell, saying: O God, whoever maintains ties with me, sever them, and whoever severs ties with me, sever them. He said: And it is about which God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. This is how it was reported. This trace is not mentioned in full.
89:15: God the Almighty says, denouncing the belief of man that if God the Almighty expands his provision to test him in that, he believes that this is from God as an honor for him, but it is not so. Rather, it is a trial and an examination, as God the Almighty said: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten to them with good things? Rather, they do not perceive. Likewise, on the other hand, if He tests him and tests him and restricts his provision, he believes that this is from God as an insult to him, as God the Almighty said: No, meaning the matter is not as he claimed, neither in this nor in that, for God the Almighty gives wealth to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, and restricts it to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love. Rather, the criterion in that is obedience to God in both cases: if he is rich, he should thank God for that, and if he is poor, he should be patient. God the Almighty’s saying: Rather, you do not honor the orphan, contains an order to honor him, as came in the hadith narrated by Abdullah bin Mubarak on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Sulayman on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Atab on the authority of Abu Abu Hurairah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The best house among the Muslims is the house in which an orphan is treated well, and the worst house among the Muslims is the house in which an orphan is treated badly. Then he pointed with his finger, I and the one who takes care of an orphan will be in Paradise like this. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah ibn Sufyan told us, Abd al-Aziz, meaning ibn Abi Hazim, told us, my father told me, on the authority of Sahl, meaning ibn Sa`id, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I and the one who looks after an orphan will be like these two in Paradise, and he joined his middle fingers and the one next to his thumb. And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor, meaning they do not command kindness to the poor and needy, nor do they urge one another to do so. And you devour inheritance, meaning the inheritance, devouring all, meaning from whatever source it came to them, whether lawful or unlawful. And you love wealth with an excessive love, meaning very much. Some of them added an obscene amount.

89:21: God Almighty tells us about the great horrors that will occur on the Day of Resurrection, as He Almighty said: No, meaning truly, when the earth is pounded to powder, meaning the earth and mountains are trampled, smoothed, and leveled, and the creation rises from their graves to their Lord, and your Lord comes, meaning to decide the judgment among His creation, after they seek His intercession through the master of the sons of Adam, Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, after they ask the messengers of resolve one after the other, and all of them say: I am not the one who can do that until the turn comes to Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he says: I am for it, I am for it, so he goes and intercedes with God Almighty that he come to decide the judgment, and God Almighty intercedes for him in that. It is the first of the intercessions and the praised station, as was explained previously in Surat Subhan. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, comes to decide the judgment as He wills, and the angels come before Him, rows upon rows. And the Almighty’s saying: And Hell will be brought forth that Day. Imam Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Umar bin Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Khalid Al-Kahili, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas’ud - who said: The Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - said: Hell will be brought forth on that Day, with seventy thousand reins, and with each rein seventy thousand angels pulling it. And this is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abdullah bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Darimi on the authority of Umar bin Hafs. And he also narrated it on the authority of Abd bin Hamid on the authority of Abu Amir on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Khalid on the authority of Shaqiq bin Salamah - he is Abu Wa’il - on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, his statement, and he did not trace it back to the Prophet. And this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Arfa on the authority of Marwan bin Mu’awiyah Al-Fazari on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Khalid on the authority of Shaqiq on the authority of Abdullah, his statement. God the Almighty says: On that Day man will remember, meaning his deeds and what he did in the past and present of his life. But how will the remembrance benefit him? “He will say, ‘Oh, would that I had sent forth [something] for my life.’” That is, he will regret what he did in the past of sins if he was a sinner, and he will wish that he had done more good deeds if he was an obedient person, as Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, meaning Ibn al-Mubarak, told us, Thawr ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umaira, who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a servant were to fall on his face from the day he was born until he dies, in obedience to God, he would despise him on the Day of Resurrection, and he would wish that he were returned to this world so that he could have more reward and recompense. God the Almighty said: On that Day, no one will punish with His punishment, meaning, no one will be more severely punished than God’s punishment of those who disobey Him, nor will anyone be bound with His bonds, meaning, no one will grip and bind with His bonds more tightly than the angels of Hell for those who disbelieve in their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. This applies to the criminals among creation and the oppressors. As for the pure and reassured soul, which is the one that is calm, steadfast, and revolves around the truth, it will be said to it: O reassured soul, * Return to your Lord, meaning to His proximity, His reward, and what He has prepared for His servants in His Paradise. Well-pleased, meaning in itself, satisfied, meaning it has been pleased with God and He has been pleased with it and has pleased it. And enter among My servants, meaning among their number, and enter My Paradise. This will be said to it at the time of death and on the Day of Resurrection as well, just as the angels give good tidings to the believer at his death and when he rises from his grave, so it is here. Then the commentators differed as to who this verse was revealed to. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan. Buraydah ibn al-Husaib narrated: It was revealed about Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib may God be pleased with him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The tranquil souls will be told on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:O tranquil soul, return to your Lord meaning your Master, which is the body that it inhabited in the world, well-pleased and pleasing. It was narrated on his authority that he used to recite: Then enter among My servants and enter My Paradise. This is what Ikrimah and Al-Kalbi said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, although it is strange. The first interpretation is more apparent because God the Almighty said: Then they will be returned to God, their True Master and And that our return is to God meaning to His judgment and to stand before Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Dashtaki told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. He said: It was revealed while Abu Bakr was sitting, so he said: O Messenger of God, how good this is. He said: This will be said to you. Then he said: Abu Sa’id Al-Ashj told us, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: I recited in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: This is good. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: The angel will say this to you at the time of death. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Ibn Yaman, and this is a good mursal. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, Marwan bin Shuja’ Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Ibn Abbas died in Taif, and a bird came that had never been seen in its form and entered his coffin, then it was not seen coming out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited on the edge of the grave, and it is not known who recited it: O reassured soul, * Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing * And enter among My servants * And enter My Paradise. Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Ahmad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Marwan bin Shuja’, on the authority of Salim bin Ajlan Al-Aftas, and he mentioned it. Al-Hafiz Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir Al-Harawi, known as Shukr, mentioned in his book, Al-Aja’ib, on the authority of Qubath bin Razin Abu Hashim, who said: “I was taken prisoner in the land of the Romans, so the king gathered us and presented his religion to us on the condition that whoever refused would be beheaded. Three apostatized, and the fourth came and refused, so his head was beheaded and thrown into a river there. It sank into the water, then it floated on the surface of the water and looked at those three and said: ‘O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so,’ calling them by their names. God Almighty said in His Book: ‘O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, And enter among My servants, And enter My Paradise.’ Then it sank into the water. He said: The Christians were about to convert to Islam, and the king’s throne fell, and those three returned to Islam. He said: A ransom came from the Caliph Abu Ja’far Al-Mansur, so we were saved.” Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Rawahah bint Abi Amr Al-Awza’i on the authority of her father: Sulayman bin Habib Al-Maharibi told me: Abu Umamah told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man: “Say: O God, I ask You for a soul that is content with You, that believes in meeting You, is pleased with Your judgment, and is satisfied with Your giving.” Then he narrated on the authority of Abu Sulayman bin Wabar that he said: This hadith of Rawahah is one of its parts, the last part of the interpretation of Surat Al-Fajr, and to God be praise and thanks.

God the Almighty said: On that Day, no one will punish with His punishment, meaning, no one will be more severely punished than God’s punishment of those who disobey Him, nor will anyone be bound with His bonds, meaning, no one will grip and bind with His bonds more tightly than the angels of Hell for those who disbelieve in their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. This applies to the criminals among creation and the oppressors. As for the pure and reassured soul, which is the one that is calm, steadfast, and revolves around the truth, it will be said to it: O reassured soul, * Return to your Lord, meaning to His proximity, His reward, and what He has prepared for His servants in His Paradise. Well-pleased, meaning in itself, satisfied, meaning it has been pleased with God and He has been pleased with it and has pleased it. And enter among My servants, meaning among their number, and enter My Paradise. This will be said to it at the time of death and on the Day of Resurrection as well, just as the angels give good tidings to the believer at his death and when he rises from his grave, so it is here. Then the commentators differed as to who this verse was revealed to. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan. Buraydah ibn al-Husaib narrated: It was revealed about Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib may God be pleased with him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The tranquil souls will be told on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:O tranquil soul, return to your Lord meaning your Master, which is the body that it inhabited in the world, well-pleased and pleasing. It was narrated on his authority that he used to recite: Then enter among My servants and enter My Paradise. This is what Ikrimah and Al-Kalbi said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, although it is strange. The first interpretation is more apparent because God the Almighty said: Then they will be returned to God, their True Master and And that our return is to God meaning to His judgment and to stand before Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Dashtaki told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. He said: It was revealed while Abu Bakr was sitting, so he said: O Messenger of God, how good this is. He said: This will be said to you. Then he said: Abu Sa’id Al-Ashj told us, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: I recited in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: This is good. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: The angel will say this to you at the time of death. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Ibn Yaman, and this is a good mursal. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, Marwan bin Shuja’ Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Ibn Abbas died in Taif, and a bird came that had never been seen in its form and entered his coffin, then it was not seen coming out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited on the edge of the grave, and it is not known who recited it: O reassured soul, * Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing * And enter among My servants * And enter My Paradise. Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Ahmad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Marwan bin Shuja’, on the authority of Salim bin Ajlan Al-Aftas, and he mentioned it. Al-Hafiz Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir Al-Harawi, known as Shukr, mentioned in his book, Al-Aja’ib, on the authority of Qubath bin Razin Abu Hashim, who said: “I was taken prisoner in the land of the Romans, so the king gathered us and presented his religion to us on the condition that whoever refused would be beheaded. Three apostatized, and the fourth came and refused, so his head was beheaded and thrown into a river there. It sank into the water, then it floated on the surface of the water and looked at those three and said: ‘O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so,’ calling them by their names. God Almighty said in His Book: ‘O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, And enter among My servants, And enter My Paradise.’ Then it sank into the water. He said: The Christians were about to convert to Islam, and the king’s throne fell, and those three returned to Islam. He said: A ransom came from the Caliph Abu Ja’far Al-Mansur, so we were saved.” Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Rawahah bint Abi Amr Al-Awza’i on the authority of her father: Sulayman bin Habib Al-Maharibi told me: Abu Umamah told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man: “Say: O God, I ask You for a soul that is content with You, that believes in meeting You, is pleased with Your judgment, and is satisfied with Your giving.” Then he narrated on the authority of Abu Sulayman bin Wabar that he said: This hadith of Rawahah is one of its parts, the last part of the interpretation of Surat Al-Fajr, and to God be praise and thanks.
